question.problem: Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points $(-1,4)$ and $(5,2).$
question.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the point $(-1,4),$ so we can use $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,4)$ in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute $m,$ and we can do this using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{2-4}{5-(-1)}=\frac{-2}{6}=-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=-\frac{1}{3}$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,4)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{1}{3}(x-(-1)) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{1}{3}(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$
